stage: Frozen after both learner views and before full drafts, author solutions, manifest or correct sets were opened.
bilingual_equivalence: Both views contain the same five question IDs, modes, figure references and 21 option IDs. Sentence-by-sentence comparison preserves outgoing small-amplitude elastic-medium scope; local motion versus disturbance/energy propagation; perpendicular/parallel direction and both examples; any versus nearest distinct in-phase points; maximum displacement and opposite phase; identical formulae; and the smallest phase-difference magnitude in radians after arrival at both balls. No additional answer cue or omitted clause changes a true set.

questions.task_fidelity: Requires the propagating disturbance definition and the distinction between local particle oscillation and energy propagation. Both must be selected; production of a free definition/explanation is not tested.
questions.redundancy: A defines the propagating phenomenon while C identifies what propagates and what remains local; they are related but not interchangeable. Combining sources 1 and 3 avoids two near-duplicate questions.
questions.answer_leakage: The stem establishes the physical regime without stating local oscillation, energy transport or a correct set. The other questions do not state A and C or whether matter travels.

option_checks.evidence: Elastic coupling causes successive particles to respond to a propagating vibrational disturbance.
A particle oscillates locally; it does not accompany the disturbance from source to far end.
Particles stay near their equilibrium locations while work by elastic forces carries mechanical energy onward.
A passing nonzero mechanical disturbance changes particle displacement and velocity; persistent rest would preclude that disturbance.
Finite propagation and the observed delayed spring-chain response imply different arrival/onset times at different distances.

questions.task_fidelity: Each response is a complete pairing of both definitions and both examples. Direction knowledge alone leaves A and D; example classification is still required. Free generation of examples is lost.
questions.redundancy: A swaps examples, B swaps direction rules, C swaps the entire type labels, and D pairs both correctly. These are distinct false procedures; no equivalent alternatives.
questions.answer_leakage: Neither the stem nor Figure 70 is attached to this item to identify the type pairing. Other questions do not supply the transverse/longitudinal definition or classify both examples.

option_checks.evidence: Direction rules are right, but traveling compressions are longitudinal and sideways cord waves transverse, so both examples are misassigned.
The cord and compression examples have the intended type labels, but transverse is not parallel and longitudinal is not perpendicular.
Parallel compression motion is internally longitudinal and perpendicular cord motion transverse; the whole type labels have been interchanged.
Sideways cord motion is perpendicular to travel (transverse); along-chain compressions have parallel motion (longitudinal).

questions.task_fidelity: Requires the nearest distinct in-phase spatial separation, discriminated from arbitrary multiples, amplitude and antiphase separation. It tests definition recognition rather than independently wording the definition.
questions.redundancy: This definition task and the figure-based numerical phase task share a concept but require different responses. A differs by a quantifier; C and D denote different physical quantities.
questions.answer_leakage: The stem does not define wavelength. Figure 70 gives a concrete wavelength span but does not state nearest, distinct or equal phase; finding the correct definition still requires the concept.

option_checks.evidence: Points separated by 2*lambda are also in phase; an arbitrary such separation is not the wavelength definition.
The smallest positive spatial separation of equal-phase points is one wavelength.
Maximum displacement from equilibrium is amplitude, not the wavelength.
Nearest antiphase points are half a wavelength apart in the harmonic traveling-wave model.

questions.task_fidelity: Tests the complete speed/wavelength/period/frequency identity without silently asserting proportionality at changing frequency. It no longer requires deriving that identity.
questions.redundancy: No other item asks for this temporal/spatial rate relation. Reciprocal, frequency-period swap and doubled-distance errors are distinct.
questions.answer_leakage: The stem identifies quantities only. Neither the phase item nor the figure explicitly gives v or the speed equation. Dimensional elimination is valid physics reasoning, not copied answer data.

option_checks.evidence: One period advances the wave one wavelength; v=lambda/T, and 1/T=nu gives lambda*nu.
T/lambda is reciprocal speed with units time/length; 1/(lambda*nu) is the same reciprocal, not v.
lambda*T=lambda/nu has units length*time rather than length/time and multiplies instead of dividing by the period.
The wave advances lambda, not 2*lambda, in T; this formula is twice the speed.

questions.task_fidelity: Requires interpreting the actual figure, counting twelve gaps, and translating the spatial fraction into phase. The smallest magnitude and arrival condition resolve sign/modulo and pre-arrival ambiguities.
questions.redundancy: Numerical phase interpretation differs from selecting a wavelength definition. The four numbers are unequal and represent distinct spacing/timing mistakes.
questions.answer_leakage: No 30-degree or pi/6 label is present in the figure or stem. The learner must use the full 2*pi cycle and count intervals. The other questions do not give the twelve-gap count or final phase.

option_checks.evidence: pi/3=2*pi/6 falsely treats the six-gap antiphase span 1-7 as a complete wavelength, doubling the actual phase step.
2*pi/13 counts thirteen balls instead of twelve intervals from ball 1 to ball 13.
lambda spans 1-13, so delta_x=lambda/12 and delta_phi=2*pi*delta_x/lambda=pi/6.
pi/2 corresponds to a T/4 temporal step between panels, not the T/12 delay between neighboring balls.

package_coverage: All six written tasks remain: definition and propagation/local-motion characteristic together; both types and examples; wavelength definition; speed relation; actual-figure phase calculation. Recognition loses independent wording, explanation, example generation and derivation, but no substantive distinction is silently omitted. No construction or new figure was required by these six sources.
